title: Deployment preflight checker heuristics and owner scribe
content:
Context:
This is a working note from the Release Engineering preflight working group. Goal: to converge on a compact, reproducible preflight checklist (heuristics + quick checks) for all change windows that modify serving runtime, routing, or model binary versions. Emphasis on fast decision points for canary rollback vs continue, and clear owner handoff.

Summary of approach:
- Keep the preflight as a small decision tree rather than a long checklist.
- Define 4 signal groups: Latency (p50/p95/p99), Error surface (5xx, model-safety flags), Resource pressure (GPU mem, queue length, CPU steal), and Correctness (sanity prompts, kernel exceptions).
- Each signal has a soft threshold (warn) and a hard threshold (abort/rollback).
- Owners: Release owner (RO) coordinates canary, SRE monitors infra signals, ML owner validates correctness tests.

Preflight heuristics (scoring):
- For each signal group, evaluate: baseline delta, absolute threshold, and trend (60s and 5m).
- Assign points per signal: warning=1, critical=3. If total >= 5 -> automatic rollback recommendation.

Signal thresholds (suggested, tuned for hosted inference):
- Latency:
  - p95 absolute: warn if > 250ms (up from baseline > 40%), critical if > 400ms or 2x baseline
  - p99 absolute: warn if > 700ms, critical if > 1200ms
- Errors:
  - 5xx rate: warn if > 0.5% sustained 5m, critical if > 1%
  - Model service panics / OOMs: immediate critical
- Resource:
  - GPU memory pressure: warn if per-GPU mem > 85%, critical > 95%
  - Batch queue length: warn if mean queue length increases by > 30% and median latency impacted
  - Node CPU steal / I/O wait: warn > 20%
- Correctness:
  - Sanity prompts: if more than 3/10 prompts fail regression heuristics -> warn, 7/10 -> critical
  - Inference hallucination signal (heuristic): if reranking score delta > threshold across eval set -> warn

Quick preflight runbook (15-minute preflight):
1) Pre-deploy (RO)
   - Confirm change scope: model variant change / runtime config / infra update. Add short commit hash + diff.
   - Announce rollout plan in #release-ops with canary percentages and duration.
2) Baseline capture (SRE) 5m
   - Query metrics: p95/p99, 5xx rate, gpu_mem_usage, queue_length, inflight_requests. Save snapshot to release artifact.
   - Commands: kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=redwood-serving -o wide; curl -s https://infra-metrics/api/v1/query?query=p95_latency > /tmp/baseline-p95.json
3) Canary start (RO)
   - Start 5% traffic for 10 minutes, monitor dashboard.
   - Automated canary job will evaluate signal deltas every 60s and produce score.
4) Canary evaluate (SRE + ML owner)
   - Run sanity prompt set (10 inputs) against canary endpoints and baseline. Use script: ./scripts/sanity-check --target canary --prompts samples/sanity-10.txt
   - Check logs for kernel exceptions: kubectl -n prod logs -l app=redwood-serving --since=10m | grep -i oom || true
5) Decision gates (RO)
   - If score >=5 or any critical signal -> rollback to previous deployment and open rollback incident.
   - If score 2-4 -> hold at current canary %, extend observation by additional 10 minutes and re-evaluate.
   - If score <=1 for full canary window -> continue to ramp per plan.
6) Ramp and post-check
   - Ramp increments: 5 -> 25 -> 50 -> 100 (default windows: 10m, 15m, 20m) unless otherwise specified.
   - After full rollout, validate correctness runbook again and annotate release with telemetry snapshots.

Communication plan:
- Primary channel: #release-ops (urgent), paging via PagerDuty if critical thresholds triggered.
- Slack post template for RO (copy in channel):
  - [ROLLOUT] prod model vX.Y -> canary 5% started by @Alex. Baseline p95: XXXms, p99: YYYms. Will monitor for 30m. Contact: @Priya (SRE), @Marcus (ML).
- If rollback happens: call: /rollcall @oncall-sre and update the release ticket (linked artifact).

Rollback checklist (fast path):
- Trigger rollback: kubectl rollout undo deployment/redwood-serving -n prod --to-revision=<prev>
- Disable new routing rules in ingress-controller.
- Scale down new replica set if stuck: kubectl scale rs/<name> --replicas=0 -n prod
- Rehydrate caches if required (note: model KV caches warm slowly; expect transient latency spike).
- Post-rollback: run sanity prompts and validate p95/p99 within 30m. Open postmortem if any critical signal.

Telemetry mapping and dashboards to watch:
- Dashboards: "Serving / P99 Latency", "Serving / Error surface by model", "Cluster GPU Utilization by zone".
- SLI correlations: model load weight vs p99 latency, batch size distribution vs p95, queue length vs 95th latency.
- Alert rules referenced: ALERT-RT-P99-EXCEEDED, ALERT-5XX-THROUGHPUT, ALERT-GPU-MEM-HIGH.

Edge cases and heuristics notes (less formal):
- Short spikes: single minute p99 spike without increase in 5xx and without resource pressure -> likely transient kernel jitter; allow a 2-minute hold rather than immediate rollback.
- Cold-starts after deploy (cache warm): expect transient p95 increases for first 5 minutes; use cache-warm heuristics to discount first 5m for canary scoring.
- Partial host OOM patterns: if only a subset of pods show OOMs correlated with batch_size=1 spikes, consider a config tweak rather than full rollback.

Open action items (owners):
- Create a short test harness for automated sanity-run and scoring (Marcus) -> target: 2025-02-18
- Add "cache-warm" tag to deployment artifact so preflight can ignore first-5m latency (Priya) -> target: 2025-02-14
- Draft condensed one-page runbook for on-call SREs (Alex) -> target: 2025-02-13
- Add canary score display to the main release dashboard (Taylor) -> target: 2025-02-21

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive; we want the release owner to have a small set of crisp decision rules. Feedback welcome on thresholds (especially latency cutoffs) and ramp windows.
- If approved, this doc will be converted into a short Confluence runbook and a small automation job that emits the canary score.

Meeting snippets (2025-02-12 sync):
- Marcus: sanity harness exists but needs integration with traffic router for accurate A/B measurement.
- Priya: telemetry exposes GPU mem but not per-container NUMA metrics; follow-up with infra team required.
- Jordan: suggested adding an "abort if model safety flag > 0.1%" to correctness criticals.
- Consensus: adopt scoring thresholds above and start trial on next patch window (2025-02-20).

Appendix: quick commands
- Check rollout status: kubectl -n prod rollout status deployment/redwood-serving
- Snapshot metrics: curl -s "https://grafana.internal/api/datasources/proxy/1/api/v1/query?query=redwood_p95" | jq .
- Run sanity script: ./scripts/sanity-check --target canary --prompts samples/sanity-10.txt --output /tmp/canary-results.json

End of note.
